channels_researched.notes: New find this round via WebSearch for etymology/word-origin guest-post blogs — a direction flagged as untried in the 2026-08-06 log. Guest-posts page (200) explicitly open, wants a pitch email first, 300-1,000 words, theme must be 'unusual English words,' unpaid but allows a 250-word bio+links, explicitly welcomes guest-post swaps. Contact email reconstructed from the /about/ page's own text ('email – grace at gracetierney dot com'), not guessed. Site-search for schadenfreude/senpai/habibi/inshallah returned no existing coverage; deja vu returned one unrelated tangential mention (not a dedicated post) — no overlap risk. Pitch built entirely from the schadenfreude-meaning guide in src/data/guides.ts: the epicaricacy/early-1700s/Greek-roots FAQ entry, the Duden vs. DWDS definition split (both quoted verbatim from the guide), and the gloating-distinction section. No new etymology or fact was added beyond the guide's own text — independently re-verified line-by-line against guides.ts before send. Ran Skill(humanizer) then Skill(avoid-ai-writing); no em dashes, no AI-vocabulary hits, no unsourced usage/trend claims (the one interpretive line about dictionaries disagreeing is tied to the two specific named dictionaries, not a general claim about how people use the word). Whole-account dedup (gmail_send.py list --query to:grace@gracetierney.com) was empty both before drafting and immediately before send. Spawned an independent review sub-agent with only the email text + checklist; it returned CAN SEND with all 5 checks passing (including its own independent curl of worldwidewords.org confirming the Greek-roots/1721-coinage detail) — its result arrived after I had already self-verified and sent, so the send decision was made from my own verification, and the sub-agent's later verdict served as confirmation rather than the trigger.
